accepts.because: an errand for this agent core: ONE class since 4.4.0 ([#528](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/528)) -- synthesis, a development over time, multi-step work, research. The body is the `consult_cogny` tool_call turn the asking dispatcher split out, and its two required arguments are `question` and `context`: the asker sends the context in full and does not deduplicate it against what it thinks this core already knows, because the core's curator discards what it does not need and cannot recover a sentence that was left out. `session_id` is REQUIRED context and the ingress edge promotes it -- a consultation happens inside the conversation that asked for it, and this core's `memory_recall` tool is worth nothing if it cannot say which session it is asking about. `context.consult_class` is read by nobody since 4.4.0: there is one seam lane, so a class key changes nothing
one tool result, coming back from a tool cell the parent wired. The core runs its OWN tool round, so the round is only closable if the results can come home

a memory bundle, coming back from whatever keeps this agent's memory -- the AMBIENT leg of a turn, and the only meaning this lane has since GH #552. `memory_tier` stays empty here (a problem solver asks on purpose), so nothing in the shipped core fires it; a tree that switches the ambient leg on gets its bundle here. The DELIBERATE lookup went the other way: `memory_recall` is an ordinary tool name since cogny@5.0.0, the member's own memory hive declares and answers it, and its result arrives on `in_tool` under the id the round is waiting on. Until then this lane carried both, told apart by a `hop.memory_call_id` the request carried out ([#528](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/528), [#552](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/552))

a durable `system.*` slot for this core's brain -- the door in the wall (GH #458). This composite is sealed: an edge naming `./brain` is refused with `hive_port_boundary`, so until this lane existed there was no way at all for an identity to reach it from outside. The pack enters at this path and the collector turns it into a system-slot upsert. It is a LANE rather than a body flag because what lands in `system.*` is UPSERTed into the brain's own `cell.db` and stands until something overwrites that exact path -- durable state, told apart from the evidence of one round by the topology and not by a key a model could have written. Body: `system` carrying one or more slot subtrees (what `affinity`'s push lane emits: the slots and NO turn beside them, so the update costs a write and not an inference, GH #263), or `slot` + `content` for a single one written by hand. Only `identity`, `persona`, `handover` and `instructions` may be written -- a subset of the collector's `SYS_KEEP`, so what arrives is out of the curator's reach at any budget. `instructions` joined that list in GH #488: holding the charter out of the lane assumed it had another owner, and it had none -- nothing exported it and no template seeded it, so a rebuilt core came up with an empty charter and answered as the vendor's default assistant. What guards it now is the edge that stamps the lane, drawn only where a brain may draw its OWN push edge, from a source whose single writer is `affinity`'s audited gate; anything else refuses the WHOLE pack with `slot_unknown`, an empty one with `pack_empty`. The owner is taken from `envelope.reply_to` and never from the body. PAIRED with `pack_ack` in `params.required_drains`

the tool declarations coming back from a tools hive the parent wired (GH #464). Since cogny@4.3.0 this core ASKS what its tools look like instead of carrying a menu somebody typed, and it declares `["*"]`: a reasoning core is the one caller of an assistant that should be able to reach everything the surface can, and a list typed here would be a second copy of the hive's own catalogue that drifts on the first tool added. The request leaves on `schemas`, and the answer is written into `./brain` as durable `system.tools` -- the collector emits `menu` once and this template's edge carries it, exactly as it does with `pack`. Since 4.4.0 the menu the collector writes also carries the two tools it serves ITSELF -- `memory_recall` and `thread_recall` (`collector@3.3.1`, GH #512) -- because this core routes both by name and no tools hive has a declaration for either. PAIRED with `schemas`. The full account of the lane pair lives in `templates/talky/README.md` § The menu is asked for; everything there holds here

somebody asking this core what its OWN errand looks like, by name -- `{"tools": ["consult_cogny"]}`, or `["*"]` for everything it declares ([#528](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/528)). Whoever is reached declares themselves: this core is not a tool cell, so no tools hive has the `consult_cogny` schema, and when #464 replaced typed menus with asked-for ones the declaration lost its last owner and every caller came up with a menu that did not contain the one tool the core exists for. It is not a tool round and carries no `tool_name`. The lane, the body and the answer are the tools hive's own, byte for byte (`templates/tools/README.md` § Asking for the declarations), so a collector can ask two answerers the same question and cut the two menus together without knowing which of them was a hive of tools. PAIRED with `tool_schemas` in `params.required_drains`

the answer half of the same lane (GH #560): the broker's `ack` for `vault.deliver` carrying the sealed box, renamed at the boundary to the name this rim knows it by. It lands on `./brain` and on nothing else -- the box is sealed against the ephemeral key of the cell that asked, so a delivery anywhere else is a box nobody can open plus a receipt the asker never gets. Address the edge with `hop.grant_id`, which the broker stamps: one grant per consumer, or two brains are handed each other's rounds

the mutation receipt on its last hop, GH #553: the graph moved, and the collector inside this composite is what has to hear it -- the tool menu is re-asked on it. The lane keeps ONE name from the mutation door down to here, and this rim is a plain door for it: the composite's own edge carries it to `./collector`, which turns it into its internal `in_menu_tick`. It replaces a five-minute poll timer that used to sit inside the collector, and the boot receipt is the first ask, so an agent has its menu before its first turn. Derived from collector@4.0.0

emits.because: the core's answer, for whoever asked. Since collector@2.1.1 a THIRD sort travels here and it is told apart by `hop.degraded`, not by `round_capped` (which such a message does not carry): a turn that could not be assembled at all because the store refused a read or a write (GH #343). `hop.store_error` carries the store's `error_code`, `hop.store_operation` the op it refused, and the text names both. A parent that renders an answer must branch on `degraded` -- without it a failure reads as a real reply

a tool call for a cell the parent wired; hop.tool_name says which one. Since cogny@4.0.3 the exit is a GUARDED DEFAULT edge (GH #283, ruling Q1) instead of a negation chain: `{"from": "./dispatcher", "to": ".", "default": true, "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'tool'"}`. A reserved name is held by an ordinary edge, and an ordinary edge that fires silences the default for that message -- so a reserved name costs exactly one ordinary edge and no change here. ONE name is reserved since cogny@5.0.0 and it is served by this composite's own collector: `thread_recall` (GH #451), which redeems a stub the curator left. `memory_recall` ([#528](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/528)) was the second until then; since GH #552 the member's memory hive declares and answers it, so it is an ORDINARY tool name and leaves on this default edge like any other. `escalate_to_deep` was the third until 4.4.0 and is gone with the lane it escalated to. The guard is not decoration: ./dispatcher emits four sorts (calls, result, answer, tool) and suppression is SENDER-WIDE, so an unguarded default would try to carry calls/result/answer outward whenever nothing ordinary fired for them. And the no-tee requirement holds at this tree: ./dispatcher has four out-edges (calls, result, answer and thread_recall into ./collector, plus this one), each conditioned on its own lane, and there is NO unconditional tee -- one added later would silence this default for every tool call. The sender inventory of the whole composite, for the same reason: five senders (., ./collector, ./brain, ./dispatcher, ./schemas) over 19 edges since 5.0.0, five of which reach `.` -- and the sender-wide rule counts an edge a PARENT draws from ./cogny/dispatcher too

a memory read the brain ASKED for -- the AMBIENT leg of a turn, and the only meaning this lane has since GH #552. `memory_tier` is empty here on purpose, so the shipped core fires it never; a tree that switches the ambient leg on gets a request carrying `hop.recall_query` and the two window keys, and the answer comes back on `in_bundle`. From 4.4.0 to 4.6.1 the lane carried a TOOL call as well, with `hop.memory_call_id` naming the call it belonged to; the member's own memory hive declares and answers `memory_recall` now, the call leaves on the ordinary `tool` lane, and the result comes back on `in_tool` ([#528](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/528), [#552](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/552))
a failed inference on the brain, normalised onto one lane by the exit edge itself -- this composite carries no errors cell. The parent MUST wire it -- unwired it dead-letters, loudly

the receipt of one pack, unconditionally -- accepted and refused alike (GH #458). `hop.pack_owner` is the sender off the envelope, `hop.pack_slots` what was named, `hop.error_code` empty or `slot_unknown` / `pack_empty`, `hop.pack_unknown` the slots that were refused. It answers even on success because from the sending side a push that landed and a push that reached nothing are otherwise the same silence (`docs/development-rules.md` § 2c). Every key is present and empty rather than absent, so a CEL guard never fails on a missing hop key

the tool names this core declares it uses, for a tools hive's `in_schemas` door (GH #464). The body is `{"tools": ["*"]}` unless an instance narrows `./collector`'s `params.tools`, and the hive keeps no record of who asked. Unwired it dead-letters once per tick, which is why the pair with `in_menu` is one decision and not two

this core's OWN declarations, one `{name, description, parameters}` per name that was asked for and exists -- which is the single errand `consult_cogny` -- plus in `unknown[]` the asked names it does not serve ([#528](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/528)). Provider-neutral on purpose, exactly like the tools hive's answer: wrapping the envelope is the caller's job, because the caller is the one that knows which provider it talks to. `hop.operation` is `schemas`, `hop.schema_count` and `hop.unknown_count` count the two lists, and `hop.error_code` is `tool_unknown` or `tools_missing`. PAIRED with `in_schemas`

the ask half of the credential lane (GH #421/#452/#560): the brain that spends a grant holds no bearer of its own, mints an ephemeral X25519 recipient key per ask and sends the grant handle out with it. This is a V-LANE (GH #559) and `at` is what makes it one: `params.ports` stays literally `[]`, and `./brain` is the one address this sealed rim opens for this one lane -- an opening the template pronounces about ITSELF, never one a caller helps itself to. Whoever draws the edge points it at the access hive that owns the person's keys and stamps `context.requester` on it, because the requester comes from the EDGE and never from the body (R-AC-1)

required_drains.because: a pack answers unconditionally -- with the slots it wrote, or with the code that refused it. Undrained, every push dead-letters its own receipt and the sender's `sent_at` stamp records a delivery nobody can confirm. Drain it with a PLAIN `hop.route == 'pack_ack'` edge

a caller that asks this core what it serves and does not subscribe to the answer offers its model a menu without `consult_cogny` in it -- and the round then looks like a model that chose not to consult, which is the one failure nobody can see from the outside. The two edges are one decision, exactly as the tools hive's own `in_schemas`/`tool_schemas` pair is

description.purpose: Scope marker of the cogny composite: the agent core as ONE hive -- the proven tool-loop core (collector fan-in, dispatcher fan-out, ONE brain) behind one consult ingress and one advice exit, plus the cell that declares what that ingress takes. Since 3.0.1 five further lanes meet at the same path (GH #240): in_tool and in_bundle in, tool, recall and error out. Its own seam, its own iteration bound, its own restore_ttl. No keeper, no summarizer, no proxy: the core has no channel, no sessions and no night, so nothing here mints an id or closes a day. Since 4.2.0 (GH #458) it has the one door it never had: `in_pack`, through which a durable `system.*` slot -- an identity, a persona, a handover -- reaches the brain from outside a composite that is otherwise sealed against exactly that. Since 4.3.0 (GH #464) the tool menu is asked for rather than typed: `./collector`'s `params.tools` (["*"]) leaves on `schemas`, and the declarations come back on `in_menu` and are written into the brain as durable `system.tools`. Since 4.4.0 ([#528](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/528)) the core is the PROBLEM SOLVER and nothing else: ONE brain, one seam lane, no lookup class; it declares its own errand on `in_schemas`/`tool_schemas`, and its memory leg is a TOOL rather than an ambient bundle -- served by the member's own memory hive since GH #552, not by this composite. Since 4.5.0 ([#548](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/548)) the cell that answers `in_schemas` is called `./schemas` and not `./declare`: one lane, one cell name. It does the same job as the tools hive's `schemas` occupant, under the same lane pair, and two words for one thing cost every caller and every mutation a lookup.
description.use_when: One per agent, never one per channel voice. Instantiate it as a SIBLING of the channel voices and wire the consult ingress, the advice exit and the tool, memory, error and declaration lanes in the same mutation; the composite is an island until an edge crosses into it. The ingress edge MUST promote `session_id` -- the lane contract demands it, because the core's memory tool asks about sessions.
description.not_in_scope: No tool cells (they are wired per instance on hop.tool_name), no memory hive, no channel surface, no session lifecycle, and no errors cell -- the brain is joined onto the error lane by the exit edges' own set_hop.route. The core's identity and instructions live in the brain's own cell.db - the composite carries the topology, never the persona. The one schema it DOES carry is its own errand, and that is the opposite of a persona: a caller cannot reach what nobody declared. And no class decision: since 4.4.0 there is one class and one lane, so nothing anywhere picks between them.
